articles.title: Court blocks DHS policy limiting international student training opportunities
articles.summary: A federal judge ruled that higher education groups challenging new Department of Homeland Security limits on the Curricular Practical Training (CPT) program are likely to succeed. As a result, the court blocked the DHS policy restricting international student training opportunities.
articles.insight:
This ruling temporarily halts U.S. restrictions on Curricular Practical Training, potentially preserving post-study work access for international students—a key factor in destination choice—though broader visa policy uncertainty and competing global pathways mean demand shifts remain contingent on enforcement and appeals.  
Admissions teams should track the legal outcome’s finality, DHS’s next steps, and comparative CPT/OPT clarity versus UK/Australia/NZ graduate work rights, while ensuring recruitment messaging accurately reflects current U.S. training eligibility without overpromising pending policy resolution.

articles.title: UK business schools report declining international enrolments and predict the downturn will persist through 2027
articles.summary: UK business schools reported declining international enrolments in the 2026 Chartered Association of Business Schools Annual Membership Survey and anticipate the downturn will continue through 2027. This trend is attributed primarily to current and forthcoming UK government policies that are complicating overseas recruitment and deterring some international students.
articles.insight:
UK business schools’ reported enrolment decline—tied to restrictive UK immigration policies—may signal softening demand from key source markets, though it remains unclear whether this reflects broader global shifts or UK-specific policy impacts.  
Admissions teams should monitor application trends from overlapping origin regions (e.g., India, Nigeria, China), track competitor messaging on visa stability, and assess whether peer institutions are adjusting recruitment tactics in response to perceived UK policy risk.

articles.title: Number of Hong Kong students in US down 27% over past 10 years
articles.summary: The number of international students from Hong Kong studying in the United States has declined by nearly 27 percent over the past decade. In the most recent school year, however, there was a slight 0.5 percent year-on-year increase, driven primarily by a 4.1 percent rise in undergraduate enrollment.
articles.insight:
The 27% decade-long decline in Hong Kong students in the US likely reflects shifting geopolitical perceptions, tightened visa scrutiny, and growing competition from other English-speaking destinations—but causality remains complex and may also involve demographic and economic factors.  
Admissions teams should monitor Hong Kong-specific application trends, visa processing times, and sentiment shifts via local education fairs and agent feedback, while assessing whether recent modest US undergraduate growth signals a potential inflection point worth targeted outreach.

articles.title: Where most international students study in the US
articles.summary: New York and California are the most popular states for international students in the United States. New York University is the top institution for international students, though both the leading states and the university are located in some of the country’s most expensive areas.
articles.insight:
New York and California’s dominance reflects enduring appeal of major urban hubs and globally ranked institutions, though high living costs may increasingly deter cost-sensitive students—especially amid tightening visa scrutiny and shifting perceptions of US affordability and safety.  
Admissions teams should track enrolment trends in high-cost states versus emerging alternatives (e.g., Texas, Florida, or midwestern universities), while assessing whether source markets are prioritising value, post-study work access, or geographic diversity over brand prestige alone.

articles.title: 15 đại học đông du học sinh nhất Mỹ
articles.summary: New York University is the university in the United States with the highest number of international students. It holds this position despite having the highest tuition fees among U.S. universities.
articles.insight:
NYU’s top ranking for international enrollment—despite its high tuition—suggests that brand prestige, urban location, and strong regional recruitment in Southeast Asia may currently outweigh cost sensitivity, though it remains unclear whether this reflects broader demand shifts or NYU-specific advantages.  
Admissions teams should track enrollment trends among Southeast Asian applicants across peer institutions, assess the impact of recent U.S. visa processing timelines and OPT policy stability, and review their own value propositions relative to NYU’s academic and experiential offerings.
